Measured coverage of realised close pairs at X = 6000: odd prime 90/751 = 12.0%, odd squarefree 128/751 = 17.0%, so the extension takes O.7 from 12.0% to 29.0%. Odd non-squarefree is a further 10.3% and satisfied the hypothesis on 77/77, but is NOT free -- rad(M) can sit far below the |V| ceiling -- so it is measured, not proved. Even M is 60.7% and is out of reach of this route entirely, since p | 2Va => p | V needs p odd. Superseded in the same way as the M_1 claim: the valuation form needs no hypothesis on M at all, so the hypotheses this claim weakens or proves are no longer on the path. Kept as true; not live.

claims.statement: Theorem O.8 assumes gcd(V,M) = 1 on each of the three pairwise steps. That is SUFFICIENT but not necessary: the three-moduli contradiction can be run at a SINGLE prime p | M, needing only p not dividing V_12, V_23 and V_13. At such a p the local subcase (whether p | S or p | T) is defined and flips at every step, so xi_1 -> xi_2 -> xi_3 returns it while xi_1 -> xi_3 flips it, and one prime suffices for the contradiction -- the whole pair (gcd(M,S), gcd(M,T)) need not swap. So the minimal hypothesis is 'some p | M divides none of the three V', which is strictly weaker than gcd(V,M) = 1.
claims.notes: What the pigeonhole buys and what it does not. PER STEP the hypothesis is FREE for M odd squarefree: if every p | M divided V then M = rad(M) | V, against 0 < |V| < M. So the dichotomy is unconditional at some prime for each step separately. It does NOT give the three-step version, because the pigeonhole can return a DIFFERENT prime for each of the three steps, and three proper subsets of the primes of M can cover them all. Making the bad sets empty -- gcd(V,M) = 1 -- is one way to force a common prime and is what O.8 assumes; requiring a common prime is another and is weaker. Empirically they do not separate: every in-window pair with M odd has gcd(V,M) = 1 (their 295/295 at X = 6000), so no realised configuration distinguishes the two hypotheses, and the weaker one is worth stating only because it is what a proof would actually have to supply. INFERRED: I derived the single-prime reduction from their statement of the argument, and have not re-derived Proposition O.6's flip at a single prime rather than mod M, which is the step that would make it real. Superseded in the same way as the M_1 claim: the valuation form needs no hypothesis on M at all, so the hypotheses this claim weakens or proves are no longer on the path. Kept as true; not live.

claims.statement: For any shared modulus m of the class (a,b), with S = X+Y and T = X-Y: S*T = -M*m. Proof: aY^2 - bX^2 = M with b = a+M gives a(Y^2 - X^2) = M(X^2+1) = M a m. Consequently, for M odd, gcd(M,S)*gcd(M,T) = M: with p^e || M, v_p(S) + v_p(T) = e + v_p(m); if p divides both S and T then p | X, so am = X^2+1 == 1 mod p and p nmid m, leaving v_p(S) + v_p(T) = e with both terms <= e.
claims.notes: 0 failures over 822,349 solutions at X = 4000 for both the identity and the factorisation, and the p|S, p|T => p|X => p nmid m step checked on all 141,277 instances. This turns O.7's dichotomy into a FACTORISATION M = M+ M- with M+ | S and M- | T, which is what lets the argument localise to composite M.

claims.statement: Theorem O.8. For M odd and SQUAREFREE, if gcd(V,M) = 1 on each of the three pairwise steps, no dyadic window contains three shared moduli. Squarefreeness makes gcd(M,S) gcd(M,T) = M a dichotomy per prime; gcd(V,M) = 1 makes the local sign defined at every p | M, so the local subcase flips at each prime and the pair (gcd(M,S), gcd(M,T)) SWAPS. Two steps restore it, one step swaps it, and M+ = M- is impossible for M squarefree > 1. Extends Theorem O.7 from M odd prime to M odd squarefree, at the cost of one hypothesis.
claims.notes: SUPERSEDED BY theorem-O9-pigeonhole, which reaches the same conclusion with NO hypothesis: the coprimality gcd(V,M) = 1 was not needed. Kept because the factorisation lemma it rests on is used by O.9, and because the conditional form was the step that made the unconditional one findable. THE HYPOTHESIS IS OBSERVED, NOT PROVED, and that is the gap. Every in-window pair with M odd has gcd(V,M) = 1 -- 295 of 295 at X = 6000, 197 of 197 at X = 4000 -- but the window bound |V| < 0.57735 M/sqrt(D) bounds V without making it coprime to M. gcd(V,M) = 1 is EQUIVALENT to g = gcd(U,V) = 1 (g | M and g | V give g | gcd(V,M); conversely p | gcd(V,M) forces p | U since U^2 = M^2 + D V^2), so it is the same quantity Prop O.1's chain tracks, where all that is known in-window is a g^2 < M, which permits g > 1. TWO CONDITIONS, NOT ONE: coprimality is what separates swap from non-swap (every non-swap has gcd(V,M) > 1; none among 1333 coprime pairs), while squarefreeness is needed so the split is a dichotomy rather than partial -- M = 9 gives (3,3), neither p^e | S nor p^e | T. A first pass recorded the non-swaps as 'all at M = 9' from an example list; the distribution is M = 3, 9, 11, 15, 21, 23, mostly squarefree. M EVEN remains outside everything here: a, b both odd makes M and V both even, so gcd(V,M) >= 2 automatically.

claims.statement: For M odd squarefree, p | M, gcd(a,M) = 1: p | V if and only if the two moduli sit in the SAME local subcase at p. Proof: a(Y^2 - X^2) = 0 mod p forces p | S or p | T; not both, since p | S and p | T give p | X, hence am = X^2+1 = 1 mod p and p does not divide m, and then S T = -M m forces v_p(S) + v_p(T) = 1 while both positive makes it >= 2. So exactly one holds and p does not divide X. Writing Y = eps X mod p with eps = -1 on p | S and +1 on p | T, V = X_i Y_j - X_j Y_i = X_i X_j (eps_j - eps_i) mod p: zero when the subcases agree, +-2 X_i X_j and nonzero when they differ. Verified: 949 (a,b,p) instances at X = 3000, 0 violations, both directions exercised (30 agree-and-divide, 919 differ-and-not), and p | X occurred 0 times.
claims.notes: Collapses two things that were being carried separately. Proposition O.6's alternation and Theorem O.8's gcd(V,M) = 1 hypothesis are the SAME statement: the subcase flips at a step precisely when p does not divide that step's V. So O.6 is not independent evidence for O.8 -- it is O.8's hypothesis, observed on the pairs where it can be observed. Built on the parallel session's S T = -M m, which is what makes the not-both step work.

claims.statement: Theorem O.8's hypothesis can be cut from three pairwise steps to two consecutive ones. If gcd(V_12, M) = gcd(V_23, M) = 1 with M odd squarefree, then by the subcase equivalence the local subcase differs across 1-2 and across 2-3, hence AGREES across 1-3, hence every p | M divides V_13, hence M | V_13 since M is squarefree -- contradicting 0 < |V_13| < 0.40825 M from the in-window bound. So no dyadic window holds three shared moduli, and nothing need be assumed about V_13.
claims.notes: A third of the hypothesis comes off, and the shape of what remains is clearer: the open question is entirely whether gcd(V,M) = 1 holds on in-window pairs, which is a statement about PAIRS -- realised, 295 of 295 at X = 6000 -- and no longer about triples, which are not realised and so cannot be swept for at all. That is the distinction the parallel session drew about O.7's measurability, arriving one level down: the hypothesis is now entirely on the observable side of it. SUBSUMED by the parallel session's Theorem O.9, which takes the same sign equivalence and needs no hypothesis at all: three signs in {+-1} cannot be pairwise distinct, so every p | M divides one of V_12, V_23, V_13 and M | V_12 V_23 V_13 for M squarefree, and the window bound then forces 3ab < M^{4/3}. My version cut the hypothesis from three steps to two; theirs removes it. Kept as true and not refuted, but it is not the live statement -- the live one is O.9.

claims.statement: Note O recorded 'the triple question has a proved unconditional constraint M/sqrt(D) >= 11.484, which is the parallel session's Plucker-parity argument'. The DERIVATION does not give that value and the constraint is not unconditional. With the exact |V| < (M/2 sqrt D)(R - 1/R), R = X_k/X_i, the stated argument (|V_ik| >= 4, R < sqrt2) gives 8 sqrt2 = 11.3137; and R < sqrt2 is only the asymptotic window condition, the exact one being R^2 < 2 + 1/X_i^2, which at X_i = 1 gives just 6.93.
claims.notes: Kept so it cannot be silently re-asserted. THE VALUE 11.484 IS CORRECT -- Theorem O.4 proves it by composition, where 2^(1/4) enters from the composite tau_1^2 < sqrt2 rather than from |V| >= 4 -- and the two expressions are algebraically identical: 4/(2^(1/4) - 2^(-1/4)) = 4(2^(1/4) + 2^(3/4)) = 11.48400. So this is a right answer with a wrong route attached, which is harder to catch than a wrong answer and was found only by deriving the same constant independently and asking why they agreed.

claims.statement: V * W = M * (m_i - m_j), where V = X_i Y_j - X_j Y_i and W = X_j Y_i + X_i Y_j. Proof: V W = X_i^2 Y_j^2 - X_j^2 Y_i^2, and Y^2 = X^2 + M m turns that into M(X_i^2 m_j - X_j^2 m_i), which with m = (X^2+1)/a is M(X_i^2 - X_j^2)/a = M(m_i - m_j) since X^2 = a m - 1. The cofactor a cancels entirely. 0 failures over 964 consecutive pairs with M odd at X = 4000. Consequences: for M odd squarefree, exactly one of V, W is divisible by each p | M, so gcd(V,M) = 1 if and only if M | W -- verified 0 failures over 744 pairs -- and the valuations are exact: v_p(V) = 1 + v_p(m_i - m_j) when the subcases agree, v_p(W) = 1 + v_p(m_i - m_j) when they differ (30 and 919 instances at X = 3000, 0 failures).
claims.notes: The cleanest form the O.8 hypothesis has taken: it is the single divisibility M | W. M | W holds 197/197 in-window at X = 4000 and only 680/767 = 88.7% out of window, so the window is doing real work rather than the divisibility being automatic. NOT proved, and the size argument does not reach it: |V| < 0.57735 M/sqrt(D), so gcd(V,M) > 1 is excluded by size only when every prime of M exceeds 0.57735 M/sqrt(D). At a = 1 that reads p > 0.577 sqrt(M), which fails for M = 33 among others -- so classes exist where nothing but the arithmetic forbids it.

claims.statement: Theorem O.9. For M = b-a odd and squarefree, a dyadic window contains three shared moduli (with X_1 >= 1) only if 3ab < (b-a)^{4/3} -- equivalently a < (t-1)^2/(3t)^{3/2} for t = b/a, so asymptotically b > 27 a^3. Proof: for p | M, aY^2 = bX^2 + M gives Y^2 == X^2 mod p and p nmid X (else p | Y so p | S and p | T, while S T = -M m with v_p(M) = 1 forces v_p(S) + v_p(T) = 1), so each solution carries a sign sigma = +-1 with Y == sigma X. Then V_ij == X_i X_j (sigma_j - sigma_i) mod p, so p | V_ij iff sigma_i = sigma_j. Three signs in {+-1} cannot be pairwise distinct, so every p | M divides one of V_12, V_23, V_13; for M squarefree that is M | V_12 V_23 V_13. In a window |V| < M/sqrt(3D), so M <= |product| < M^3/(3D)^{3/2}. Recovers Theorem O.7 for M prime with NO hypothesis, and supersedes O.8's coprimality assumption.
claims.notes: SUPERSEDED BY theorem-O10-valuation, which drops the odd and squarefree hypotheses entirely by replacing the two-valued sign with a valuation split s + t >= e. Kept because the sign is the e = 1 shadow of that and is how the argument was found. NOT A WEAK CONDITION: at X = 4000, 499,188 of 503,054 classes with M odd squarefree (99.2%) fail 3ab < M^{4/3} and are excluded outright. With O.4's t > 133.875 the admissible a is tiny -- a <= 2 at the minimum admissible t, 6 at t = 1e3, 19 at t = 1e4. Verified at X = 4000: 0 failures over 1,588,226 sign determinations and 1317 (p,pair) equivalence checks; 0 failures of M | V12 V23 V13 over the realised triples; 0 failures of |V| < M/sqrt(3D) over 139 in-window pairs. THE CLEANER IDENTITY IS THE PARALLEL SESSION'S: V W = M (m_i - m_j) with W = X_j Y_i + X_i Y_j -- mine divided by a, and the cofactor cancels entirely (0 failures over 2747 pairs). It also gives gcd(V,M) = 1 <=> M | W for M odd squarefree. STILL OPEN: M even and M non-squarefree, where sigma is undefined -- at M = 9 the pair (gcd(M,S), gcd(M,T)) is (3,3) and p | X becomes possible.

claims.statement: For M = b - a odd, V = X_i Y_j - X_j Y_i is always even. M odd means a and b are not both 2 mod 4. If a and b are both odd then m must be odd -- m even would give am and bm even, so X and Y both odd, so a = b = 2 mod 4 is not needed but M = b-a even, a contradiction -- and then X^2 = am-1 and Y^2 = bm-1 are both even, so X and Y are both even. If a = 2 mod 4 and b is odd then m is odd, X^2 = am-1 is odd and Y^2 = bm-1 is even, so X is odd and Y even. Either way every term of V has an even factor. Verified over all consecutive pairs at X = 4000: 0 odd |V| out of 2566.
claims.notes: Small and load-bearing: it turns |V| < 4 into |V| = 2, which is what makes the Plucker threshold prove O.8's hypothesis rather than merely bound V.

claims.statement: O.8's hypothesis gcd(V,M) = 1 is a THEOREM, not an observation, whenever M/sqrt(D) <= 8/(sqrt r - 1/sqrt r) with r = 2 + 1/X_i^2 -- i.e. 4 sqrt 3 = 6.9282 at X_i = 1, rising to 8 sqrt 2 = 11.3137. Chain, all proved: the bound |V| < (M/2 sqrt D)(sqrt r - 1/sqrt r) from V W = M(m_i - m_j) and Y > X sqrt(b/a); V even for M odd; V nonzero. So below the threshold |V| < 4 forces |V| = 2, and gcd(2,M) = 1. Coverage at X = 4000: 234 of 498 in-window pairs (47.0%) are below the threshold and ALL have |V| = 2; 95 of those have M odd and all have gcd(V,M) = 1 by the argument rather than by measurement.
claims.notes: The Plucker bound and O.8's hypothesis turn out to be the same inequality read in opposite directions. The parallel session had just corrected the bound's derivation -- it gives 8 sqrt 2, not 11.484 -- and treated it as a constraint on TRIPLES; used as a constraint on a single step it proves the pair-level hypothesis outright below the threshold. Above it, |V| >= 4 becomes possible and the hypothesis is open: measured 0 counterexamples over 295 in-window M-odd pairs at X = 6000 and 451 at X = 9000, and the only in-window pairs with |V| > 2 anywhere in the data -- |V| = 24, 66, 182 at (53,423125), (1,51701), (1,423125) -- all have M EVEN, hence gcd(V,M) >= 2 automatically and nothing to prove. Superseded in the same way as the M_1 claim: the valuation form needs no hypothesis on M at all, so the hypotheses this claim weakens or proves are no longer on the path. Kept as true; not live.

claims.statement: Theorem O.9 generalises off M odd squarefree and reaches M EVEN. Nothing in the sign argument is about M -- it is about a single odd prime p with p || M, which is what makes the sign well defined (p | S and p | T would give p | X, and S T = -M m with v_p(M) = 1 forces v_p(S) + v_p(T) = 1). Let M_1 = product of the odd primes p with p || M. Each such p divides one of V_12, V_23, V_13 since three signs in {+-1} cannot be pairwise distinct; M_1 is squarefree, so M_1 | V_12 V_23 V_13; and |V| < M/sqrt(3D) gives M_1 < M^3/(3D)^{3/2}. Hence a dyadic window holds three shared moduli only if 3ab < (M^3/M_1)^{2/3}. For M odd squarefree M_1 = M and this is O.9's 3ab < M^{4/3}. Coverage, on the only population where the statement is not vacuous -- classes with at least 3 shared moduli, since fewer than 3 cannot host a triple whatever any theorem says: at X = 3000 there are 60 such classes out of 1,815,154, and the bound excludes 9 (15.0%), leaves 30 admissible (50.0%), and is silent on 21 (35.0%, M_1 = 1). Restricted further to M odd squarefree, where the bound is O.9's own 3ab < M^{4/3}, it excludes 6 of 11. Zero classes have three moduli in one dyadic window at this X.
claims.notes: The hypothesis 'M odd squarefree' was doing two jobs and only one of them was needed. Squarefreeness of M is used nowhere: what is used is v_p(M) = 1 at the single prime being worked at, and M_1 collects exactly those primes. Oddness of M is not needed either -- only oddness of p. Verified on M EVEN specifically, which is the new range: sign well defined, p never divides X, and p | V iff the signs agree, over 200+ (pair, p) instances at X = 2000. The conclusion is a configuration that does not occur, so only the hypotheses are checkable; they are checked on pairs, which do occur. COVERAGE FIGURES CORRECTED, and the first version was the repo's own trap. I reported '95.68% of classes excluded outright, silent on 1.02%' over ALL 1,815,154 classes -- of which 1,815,094 have FEWER THAN 3 MODULI and cannot host a triple regardless. So 99.997% of that denominator was vacuous and both figures were meaningless as stated. On the 60 classes that could host one, the bound excludes 15% and is silent on 35%. The rule this repo already carries -- the informative subset is never the one the loop naturally counts -- and I wrote a sweep over every class because every class is what ratio_classes returns. The THEOREM is unaffected; only its advertised reach was. SUPERSEDED by the parallel session's p-adic valuation form, which drops every hypothesis on M rather than weakening one: s_i = min(e, v_p(S_i)), t_i = min(e, v_p(T_i)), s_i + t_i >= e, and ordering by s gives M | V_12 V_13 V_23 with no M_1 and no restriction to v_p(M) = 1. My version reached the same conclusion on the primes that exactly divide M; theirs reaches it on all of them, because when p | X the split simply puts weight on both s and t and the ordering still works. Kept as true and correctly derived, but it is not the live statement. The sequence -- their M odd squarefree, my odd p || M, their full valuation form -- is three passes at the same argument, each removing a hypothesis the previous one had thought structural.

claims.statement: Theorem O.10. For ANY M = b-a -- odd or even, squarefree or not -- M | V_12 V_23 V_13 for three shared moduli of a class; hence, since a dyadic window gives 0 < |V| < M/sqrt(3D), a window holds three only if 3ab < (b-a)^{4/3}. Proof: gcd(a,M) = 1, and for p^e || M, b == a mod p^e with aY^2 = bX^2 + M gives Y^2 == X^2 mod p^e, i.e. p^e | S T (Lemma S T = -M m). With s_i = min(e, v_p(S_i)) and t_i = min(e, v_p(T_i)) we get s_i + t_i >= e; p^{s_i} | S_i gives Y_i == -X_i mod p^{s_i} and p^{t_i} | T_i gives Y_i == X_i mod p^{t_i}, either of which kills V_ij, so v_p(V_ij) >= max(min(s_i,s_j), min(t_i,t_j)). Ordering s_1 <= s_2 <= s_3 gives v_p(V_23) >= s_2 and v_p(V_12) >= e - s_2, so their sum is >= e.
claims.notes: SHARPENED BY theorem-O11-coupled-ratios, which uses R_12 R_23 = R_13 to replace the constant 1/3 by 0.048628 -- 6.85x -- and lifts the informative coverage from ~35% to 88-98%. O.10's divisibility M | V12 V23 V13 is what O.11 rests on. THE SIGN IS THE e = 1 SHADOW: at v_p(M) = 1, S T = -M m forces s + t = 1 exactly, so (s,t) is (1,0) or (0,1), which is sigma = -+1. 'Three signs in {+-1} collide' becomes 'order by s and take the middle two', and that is the only step that changes. NO CASE REMAINS: O.9 needed M odd squarefree and the parallel session's intermediate M_1 = prod{odd p || M} form left 1.02% of classes silent (M a power of two times a powerful odd part); the valuation form covers those and excludes 99.2% of them. COVERAGE, WITH ITS DENOMINATOR. A first version reported '99.26% of classes excluded', which is over EVERY ratio class -- and a class with fewer than three shared moduli cannot host a triple at all. At X = 3000 only 60 of 1,815,154 classes have three shared moduli, so that figure measured vacuity, not reach. On the INFORMATIVE population it is ~35% and stable: 17/48 (35.4%) at X = 2000, 21/60 (35.0%) at 3000, 24/70 (34.3%) at 4000, 34/96 (35.4%) at 6000. The gain over the M_1 form survives: on the same 60 classes it excludes 21 with none silent, against 9 excluded and 21 silent. Found by the parallel session in its own figures and applying identically here. Verified 0 failures at X = 4000 over 12,447,219 checks of s + t >= e, 6266 of the v_p(V) bound, 224 of the ordered two-term sum, and M | V12 V23 V13 on every realised triple in all categories (odd squarefree 23, odd non-squarefree 39, even non-squarefree 216).

claims.statement: The sign argument needs an odd p | M, so it is silent on M a pure power of two, and those classes are the modulus-rich ones. Share of classes with M = 2^e: at X = 3000, 0.013% of all classes, 8.3% of classes with >= 3 shared moduli, 16.7% with >= 4, 50.0% with >= 5; at X = 6000, 0.004%, 6.2%, 15.4%, 33.3%. A 600x to 4000x enrichment, stable across a doubling of X. The single richest class in the data -- (1,5), M = 4, eight shared moduli 2, 10, 65, 442, 3026, 20737, 142130, 974170 -- is one, and so are (1,17) and (1,65): these are b = 2^e + 1 with a = 1, the Pell chains.
claims.notes: The reason the reach figures needed correcting twice. By class count the blind spot is negligible; on the population that could host a triple it is 35%, and among the richest classes it is half. So it is not a uniform residue to be mopped up later -- it is concentrated on exactly the configurations where a counterexample would live, and the correlation is not weak. Recorded as `rigorous_finite` at two sizes rather than extrapolated: the enrichment is stable but no law is fitted to it, and the counts at >= 5 moduli are 6 and 9, which is too few to fit anything to. SUPERSEDED IN SIGNIFICANCE, though the measurement stands. The parallel session's p-adic valuation form of the sign argument drops every hypothesis on M -- s_i = min(e, v_p(S_i)), t_i = min(e, v_p(T_i)), s_i + t_i >= e, and ordering by s gives the two needed terms -- so the silent class is CLOSED, not merely reduced, and goes from 35.0% of informative classes to 0. The enrichment figures remain true as facts about where M = 2^e and M_1 = 1 sit in the population; what is no longer true is the reading that they mark where the remaining work is. They do not: the remaining work is the 39 of 60 informative classes that are ADMISSIBLE under 3ab < M^{4/3} and hold no triple anyway.

claims.statement: The valuation argument's per-prime conclusion v_p(V_12) + v_p(V_23) >= e does NOT give M | V_12 V_23 for any fixed pair, because the s-ordering that selects the pair is computed per prime and different primes select different pairs. Only the three-term product is uniform: M | V_12 V_13 V_23. Counterexamples exist: 5 of 216 realised triples at X = 3000 admit NO single pair whose product is divisible by M -- (1,481) M=480 moduli 2,1157,17690; (1,925) M=924 moduli 2,5,7922; (1,106) M=105 moduli 5,65,4097; (1,2465) M=2464 moduli 10,37,530; (1,1450) M=1449 moduli 17,65,901 -- all with M carrying three or more distinct primes. The per-prime statement itself holds: 216 of 216 triples, 0 failures.
claims.notes: Recorded because the two-term version would CLOSE Conjecture O.2 outright and it is the obvious next move. If M | V_a V_b for a fixed in-window pair, then M <= |V_a V_b| < M^2/(3D) gives 3ab < M = b - a, which is impossible for a >= 1 since 3ab >= 3b > b - a. I derived exactly that and was one step from asserting the conjecture proved. The quantifier is what fails: the pair depends on p. The three-term product gives only 3ab < M^{4/3}, which is satisfiable. This is the 'right answer with a wrong route' shape caught before the assertion rather than after -- and it was caught by asking which objects the quantifier ranges over, not by any number coming out wrong, since every number in the per-prime check was correct.

claims.statement: Theorem O.11. Since R_12 R_23 = R_13, the three per-pair bounds |V_ij| < (M/sqrt D) sinh(u_ij) cannot all sit at the window's edge. For fixed u_13, sinh(u_12) sinh(u_23) is maximised at the equal split u_12 = u_23 = u_13/2 (derivative sinh(u_13 - 2u_12)), so f(R_12) f(R_23) f(R_13) <= 16 sinh^3(u/2) cosh(u/2) = (sqrt rho - 1/sqrt rho)^3 (sqrt rho + 1/sqrt rho) =: C(X_1) with rho = sqrt(2 + 1/X_1^2). With M <= |V12 V23 V13| that gives ab < (C(X_1)/8)^{2/3} (b-a)^{4/3}: 0.125873 at X_1 = 1 falling to 0.048628 asymptotically, against O.10's 1/3 -- 6.85x stronger.
claims.notes: COVERAGE, WITH ITS POPULATION AND ITS TREND. Over classes with >= 3 shared moduli -- the only ones that could host a triple -- O.11 excludes 42/43, 46/48, 57/60, 65/70, 88/96, 96/109 at X = 1500, 2000, 3000, 4000, 6000, 8000, i.e. 97.7%, 95.8%, 95.0%, 92.9%, 91.7%, 88.1%. DO NOT READ THAT AS AN ASYMPTOTIC: O.10's ~35% is flat in X while O.11's falls monotonically, and the admissible count roughly doubles as X doubles (1, 2, 3, 5, 8, 13) while the informative population grows only 2.5x over that range. The reach may tend to 0 and no claim is made about its limit. The equal-split maximisation was confirmed numerically to eight digits over a 4000-point grid at four values of w.

claims.statement: Theorem O.11's constant, re-derived and cross-checked. With R_ij = e^{u_ij} the bound |V_ij| < (M/2 sqrt D)(R - 1/R) is |V_ij| < (M/sqrt D) sinh(u_ij), and R_12 R_23 = R_13 means u_12 + u_23 = u_13, so sinh(u_12) sinh(u_23) is maximised at the equal split -- the derivative is sinh(u_13 - 2 u_12), zero exactly at u_12 = u_13/2 and changing sign there. Hence the triple product is < (M/sqrt D)^3 * 2 sinh^3(u/2) cosh(u/2) = (M/sqrt D)^3 K/8 with K = (sqrt rho - 1/sqrt rho)^3 (sqrt rho + 1/sqrt rho), rho = sqrt(2 + 1/X_1^2). M <= product then gives ab < (K/8)^{2/3} M^{4/3}. Computed: K/8^{2/3} = 0.125873 at X_1 = 1, 0.049344 at X_1 = 10, 0.048628 asymptotically; against O.10's 1/3 that is 6.855x. The sinh form and the sqrt-rho form agree to 6 places (0.010723 both).
claims.notes: Verified by re-deriving rather than re-running. The step worth checking was the maximisation, since 'all three R at the window edge' is exactly the over-count O.10 makes and the constraint R_12 R_23 = R_13 is what forbids it; the derivative sinh(u_13 - 2u_12) is clean and the equal split is a genuine maximum. I got 0.1421 on the first pass by using 0.5946 for 2^{1/4} - 2^{-1/4} instead of 0.34831 -- their number is right and mine was an arithmetic slip. Their trend caveat is the important half: the reach 97.7 -> 88.1% is FALLING over X = 1500 to 8000 with the admissible count doubling per doubling of X, so no limit is claimed and none should be.

claims.statement: `rational-gram-bounded-on-windows` and Note O's Conjecture O.2 are the same statement. The off-diagonal Gram entry of the rational graph restricted to a dyadic window [N,2N) is the number of moduli in that window shared by a cofactor pair (a,b); O.2 says no dyadic window contains three shared moduli. So 'max windowed Gram entry is 2' IS 'no window holds three', with no translation. Verified directly: max shared moduli in one dyadic window is 2 at X = 2000 and 4000, attained at (1,41) with moduli 730 and 1370, and zero classes hold three.
claims.notes: This is why the Note O thread is not a side quest. `rational-gram-bounded-on-windows` is `rigorous_finite` -- 'uniformly for X <= 8000' -- and it is what Note L's conclusion rests on, that merging rows over Z thickens each side separately and never jointly. Theorems O.9 and O.11 prove exactly that bound on the classes satisfying 3ab < M^{4/3} and its sharpened form, so the Note O work is PROMOTING a central finite measurement of Note L toward a theorem for all X. NOT NEW, and my commit message claiming 'neither note said so' was false. Note L's section 'What proving the triple statement would actually buy' states it outright -- "'No dyadic window holds three' is exactly G'(n1,n2) restricted to a window <= 2" -- and says it would move `rational-gram-bounded-on-windows` from rigorous_finite to proved. I wrote that section. I re-derived it, asserted it was a connection neither note had drawn, and sent it to the parallel session as new. The identification stands; the novelty did not. AND NOTE L IS MORE CAREFUL THAN THIS CLAIM WAS. It adds that proving it upgrades one claim's STATUS and changes no conclusion -- the argument uses only that there is no main term to extract, and a bounded count supplies none at 1, 2 or 3 alike -- and it warns that the O.2 work 'reads, from the volume of it, like something with more at stake'. The parallel session's `triple-question-upgrades-status-not-conclusion` matches Note L exactly, and my message to them calling this 'a stronger framing than upgrades-status-not-conclusion' had it backwards: theirs was the careful reading and mine was the inflated one. Partial, not complete: O.11's measured reach is falling with X, so what is proved is a shrinking share of the classes, and the promotion is not yet available. The identification is definitional -- it is about what the two statements SAY -- so it does not depend on the measurement, and the dependency guard rejected the edge I first wrote to `rational-gram-bounded-on-windows`. That is the third time tonight it has caught the same habit: listing the neighbouring result as a premise because it is the thing the claim is ABOUT. A claim about X is not a claim resting on X, and the ordering rule is what keeps the two apart.

claims.statement: Every ratio class that Theorem O.11 admits, among those holding >= 3 shared moduli, has a = 1. Across X = 1500, 2000, 3000, 4000, 6000, 8000 there are 9, 12, 16, 19, 30, 33 informative classes with a >= 2 -- 119 in total -- and O.11 excludes EVERY one, while the a = 1 admitted counts are 1, 2, 3, 5, 8, 13. This matters because full-graph-growth-is-pell records that n1 = 1 cannot occur in a Type II hypothesis, where both variables are confined to ranges: so on the classes the Type II question actually ranges over, O.11 is currently exhaustive.
claims.notes: A RANGE EFFECT, NOT A LAW, and the law is easy to write down: O.11 admits (a,b) as soon as ab < c (b-a)^{4/3}, and for FIXED a the right side wins as b -> infinity. The crossover is b ~ 9.0e3 at a = 1, 7.0e4 at a = 2, 2.4e5 at a = 3, 1.1e6 at a = 5. So the a >= 2 column is empty because the sweep does not reach far enough in b, and it WILL fill in at larger X -- the a = 1 column is already filling. Recorded with the crossover values precisely so the finite reading cannot be mistaken for a structural one; this is the same failure the denominator correction was about, anticipated rather than repaired.

claims.statement: That O.11 excludes every informative class with a >= 2 is a RANGE effect and not a structural fact, confirmed independently. O.11 admits (a,b) once ab < 0.048628 (b-a)^{4/3}, so for fixed a the right side wins as b grows; crossover b is ~9e3 at a = 1, ~7e4 at a = 2, ~2.37e5 at a = 3, ~1.13e6 at a = 5 -- reproduced to the digits given. But the largest b among informative classes with a >= 2 is 925 at X = 3000 and 8321 at X = 6000, an order of magnitude below the a = 2 crossover. So the a >= 2 column is empty because the sweep cannot reach it, and the data cannot test the question at all. The single admissible class at X = 6000 is (1, 18241), which sits above the a = 1 crossover exactly as predicted.
claims.notes: Worth keeping because of how it was caught rather than what it says. A column of zeros that is going to fill looks identical to a column of zeros that is a law, and neither the population check nor the >90% check separates them -- only the direction of travel does, which is the third layer of the percentage rule and the one the parallel session added. They anticipated the failure and recorded the crossover values inside the claim so the finite reading cannot be mistaken for a structural one; I confirmed the crossovers and then measured the largest b actually available, which is the part that settles it. Note the near-miss underneath: a = 1 means the unit cofactor, which no Type II hypothesis admits, so 'O.11 is exhaustive on the classes Type II ranges over' was available as a headline and would have been false for range reasons alone.

claims.statement: Theorem O.12. If n_2/n_1 < (5+sqrt21)/2 = 4.7913 -- in particular if n_1 and n_2 lie in ONE DYADIC BAND -- then they share at most one modulus in any dyadic window. So the rational incidence graph restricted to the doubly-dyadic configuration (cofactors banded, moduli windowed) is C_4-FREE. Proof: a pair of shared moduli m_i < m_j < 2 m_i with X_i >= 1 needs tau_V^2 < 2 + 1/X_i^2 <= 3; tau increases in |V| and |V| >= 1, so tau_V >= tau(1) = sqrt(1+s^2) + s with s = sqrt(D)/M, and tau(1)^2 < 3 forces M/sqrt(D) > sqrt3. With u = n_2/n_1 = b/a, M/sqrt(D) = (u-1)/sqrt(u), and that exceeds sqrt3 iff u^2 - 5u + 1 > 0 iff u > (5+sqrt21)/2. A dyadic band gives u < 2, a factor 2.4 inside.
claims.notes: WHY IT MATTERS OUTSIDE NOTE O. gaussian-to-rational-bridge is `inferred` and its stated gap is 'what is proved over Z[i] is G <= 1; what is measured over Z is G' <= 2 on every dyadic window for X <= 8000'. Ford-Maynard's (II) is bilinear over m ~ M and n ~ N, so BOTH variables are banded -- fm-barrier-range-is-small-moduli records that footnote 2 averages over m_1, m_2 ~ x^{1-2c+eps}. On that configuration O.12 proves G' <= 1 over Z for all X, matching the Z[i] bound exactly rather than being a measured constant one larger. WHAT IT DOES NOT CLOSE: the bridge's remaining inference, 'both give no main term, so the conclusion is unchanged', is untouched -- O.12 removes the quantitative discrepancy and the finite floor, not the reasoning. And it says nothing about O.2, the free-cofactor question: (1,41) shares 730 and 1370, a genuine G' = 2, with 41/1 = 41 far outside one band. Measured at X = 2000, 3000 and 6000: banded max Gram 1 at every dyadic modulus window, free max Gram 2. Uses |V| >= 1 rather than the parity lemma's |V| >= 2, so it is independent of the parity of a and b. POSITIVE CONTROL, since a 'max of 1' over pairs that share nothing would look identical and mean nothing: at X = 3000 over 300,026 banded cofactor pairs, 57,132 share exactly one modulus and 0 share two or more, while 127 FREE pairs share two. The forbidden configuration occurs the moment the banding is dropped, so the sweep is not vacuous and the hypothesis is what is doing the work. NOT KNIFE-EDGE: the proved threshold 4.7913 uses only |V| >= 1; with |V| >= 2 (the parity lemma, whenever M is odd) it rises to 13.9282 at X_1 = 1 and 33.9706 asymptotically. Empirically the minimum n_2/n_1 among pairs sharing two moduli in one window is 43.79 at (34,1489) with moduli 1073 and 1973, over 125 such pairs at X = 3000 -- 9.1x the proved bound. So the theorem covers any reasonable reading of 'both variables in ranges', not only the dyadic one.

claims.statement: Note K's line result and Note L's degree ladder are the same fact seen from the two sides. N(a+ci) = a^2 + c^2, so a LINE in Z[i] is a degree-2 single-variable sequence over Z; Note L's ladder gives kappa = X^{2-d}, hence kappa = 1 exactly at d = 2, and Note K gives kappa = 1 - c^2/Q -> 1 for every line. The geometry is the explanation of the exponent: a line's count is its length, and its length is sqrt(Q). On the Z side the family is uniform too -- with windows normalised to each sequence's own sqrt(Q), the max off-diagonal Gram excluding the unit modulus is 2 at [sqrt Q, 2 sqrt Q) and [sqrt Q/2, sqrt Q) for every c = 1,2,3,5,7,11,13 at X = 3000, with occasional 3s only at sqrt(Q)/8 and below.
claims.notes: NORMALISATION TRAP, recorded because I nearly published the opposite. Measured on FIXED windows [64,256) the same quantity reads 2,3,3,3,4,5,6 across c = 1..13, which says the Z-vs-Z[i] gap widens with c and that x^2+1 is unusually tight -- an attractive finding and false. A fixed window sits at a different depth in each sequence's value range, since x^2+c^2 starts at 1+c^2; normalising the window to each sequence's own sqrt(Q) removes the effect almost entirely. The repo's normalisation rule already says to state which quantity an exponent is relative to; this is the same rule for a WINDOW, across sequences, where it is easier to miss because the window looks like an absolute range.

claims.statement: The C4-free obstruction holds in BOTH formulations on the configuration a Type II hypothesis quantifies over, so it does not depend on the choice of ring. Note F proves G <= 1 over Z[i] for all cofactor pairs; Theorem O.12 proves G' <= 1 over Z for cofactors within a factor 4.7913, in particular within one dyadic band, on every dyadic modulus window. [FM]'s (II) is bilinear over m ~ M and n ~ N, so only banded pairs occur in it. Hence the numerical input to nu = 0 is available over Z directly and does not have to be carried across from Z[i]. The repo's headline -- the obstruction is a theorem about the sequence and survives any change of sieve -- extends to: it survives the change of ring as well, on the configuration that matters.
claims.notes: INFERRED, and the inferred part is narrow and named: that [FM]'s (II) sees only banded cofactor pairs. That is a reading of their quantifier, the same reading `gaussian-to-rational-bridge` rests on, and it is not proved here. Everything else is proved -- Note F by the two-line argument over Z[i], O.12 by the Pell/window argument over Z. SCOPE, since 'the Gaussian formulation is not needed' would be too strong: it is not needed FOR THIS STEP. Z[i] remains the repo's working setting for the Type I analysis, the factorisation machinery, and the sieve setup, and O.12's own proof runs on x^2+1's Pell structure rather than on anything ring-free. What changes is that the C4-free input to the Type II conclusion no longer arrives through a bridge; it is available on both sides.
